title: Notifications API + weekly digest job
pr_description: Exposes notifications over the API (list unread, mark read) and adds send_weekly_digests(), the scheduled job that mails every user a spending digest for the month and tidies up their notification list.

defects.description: GET /notifications honors a user_id query parameter over the authenticated user — a debugging convenience left in. Any logged-in user can read any other user's notifications (which contain their budget and spending details) by passing ?user_id=N.

After queuing a digest the job marks ALL of the user's notifications read — not just digests. Any unread over-budget alert the user hasn't seen yet is silently swallowed by the weekly job. The update must filter on kind = 'digest' (or better, only the row it just created).

POST /notifications/read updates by notification id alone, bypassing notify.mark_read's user scoping that exists precisely for this. Any user can mark any other user's notifications read (suppressing their over-budget alerts) by guessing ids.

defects.anchor: assert any(n["kind"] == "digest" for n in unread(db, user)) or True
defects.description: The added digest test is unfalsifiable: 'or True' makes the first assertion a tautology and the second ('count <= 1') passes on an empty list. It therefore never notices that digests are queued already-read (the job's own UPDATE swallows them), which is why CI stays green.
